# SEC filing-index ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). | uv workspace of four packages (root `pyproject.toml`).
Ranking: your partner's, 2026-11-06 — the listed order.

| # | Outcome | Spec | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Filing-index rows for every archived quarter in a configured range | §2.1, §4.2, R1 | A | 1 | 2 requests per quarter (listing + master.idx), under 1 s each at 3 req/s; volume per quarter measured by Stage 1, total = that × quarters in range |
| O2 | Daily indexes added as they appear, catching up after missed runs | §2.1, §4.2, R2 | A | 2 | About 1 file + 1 listing per business day, about 250/year; size per file measured by Stage 1 |
| O3 | One canonical filing-index dataset in Parquet, one row per filing | §4.5, §4.6, R3 | A | 3 | Measured by Stage 1 (rows, bytes, elapsed, peak memory for one quarter) |
| O4 | The runs execute on Azure: ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, Monitor | §4.1, §4.9, R4 | A | 4 | Azure spend unknown until resource sizes are chosen; measured by the Stage 7 smoke test |
| O5 | Backfill, daily and reconciliation share one downloader, parser and publisher | §4.1, R5 | A | 5 | Engineering time only |
| O6 | A parser change reprocesses stored source bytes with no new SEC download | §4.5, §4.6, R6 | A | 6 | Storage = raw bytes retained; sized from Stage 1's per-quarter bytes |
| O7 | Quarterly indexes re-read on a schedule, additions and changes recorded | §4.2, §4.4, R7 | A | 7 | Weekly: 2 requests × quarters in range, plus re-transform of changed quarters only; transform time from Stage 1 |
| O8 | All SEC traffic shares one request budget, however many workers run | §4.3, R8 | A | 8 | Caps throughput at 3 req/s total (§4.8) |
| O9 | Readers get only complete quarter generations, through one active pointer | §4.5, §4.6, R9 | A | 9 | Storage grows with retained generations; retention set at deployment |
| O10 | Records leave the catalog only after approval bound to the source hash | §4.4, R10 | A | 10 | Your partner's time per gated closed-quarter candidate |
| O11 | Schedules, retry limits and the rate target live in reviewed configuration | §4.8, R11 | A | 11 | Not material |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: One real quarter to canonical Parquet
      Objective: Fetch one archived quarterly index and one published daily index from the SEC and parse them into the canonical row contract as local Parquet.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: nothing (generated package scaffolds only)
      Produces: a parser and polite single-process fetcher (identifying User-Agent, 3 req/s); `sec-index-v1` rows in local Parquet; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O3 — Parquet for one archived quarter and one daily index passes the §4.5 row contract with duplicate keys collapsed; the findings file records byte counts, row counts, elapsed time, peak memory and observed request rate of the real run
      Leaves out: manifests (Stage 2); point-in-time awareness (Stage 4); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7); full validation suites (Stage 8); traceability (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Raw snapshots, manifests and replay
      Objective: Retain original bytes content-addressed and track source, snapshot and processing state so any stored source can be reprocessed offline through one shared command path.
      Outcomes: O5, O6
      Consumes: Stage 1 parser and fetcher
      Produces: manifests (§4.5 Source, Snapshot, Workset binding, Processing, Attempt records); `discover`/`collect`/`transform`/`publish` commands over a storage interface
      Exit: O5 — quarterly and daily sources run through the same four commands; O6 — a parser-version change rebuilds output from stored bytes with zero SEC requests and the same logical rows
      Leaves out: Azure storage backends (Stage 7); point-in-time awareness (Stage 4)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Backfill range and daily catch-up
      Objective: Ingest a configured quarter range and discover daily indexes from listings, resuming after missed runs.
      Outcomes: O1, O2
      Consumes: Stage 2 manifests and commands
      Produces: range backfill and daily discovery with per-source-file checkpoints and complete/pending/failed reporting
      Exit: O1 — an inclusive quarter range ingests with each unit reported complete, pending or failed; O2 — a run after a missed span crossing a quarter boundary picks up every listed unprocessed file and reports `no_new_sources` on an unchanged listing
      Leaves out: the full historical campaign (Stage 9); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: Quarter generations and active pointer
      Objective: Publish each affected quarter as an immutable generation behind a conditionally updated pointer.
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 2 manifests; Stage 3 ingested sources
      Produces: point-in-time awareness (per-quarter generations, manifest.json, changes.parquet, active pointer)
      Exit: O9 — a crash injected before the pointer update leaves the prior generation readable, and a competing publisher's stale build cannot overwrite a newer pointer
      Leaves out: withdrawal gating (Stage 5)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Reconciliation and withdrawal gate
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes, publish safe changes, and hold key removals for hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stage 4 generations and pointer
      Produces: a reconciliation workflow; approval records; `awaiting_approval` candidates
      Exit: O7 — a changed quarterly snapshot publishes its additions and field updates with a change report; O10 — a closed-quarter candidate that removes keys stays inactive until an approval names its exact hash, and stale daily replay cannot resurrect an approved withdrawal
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Shared SEC request budget
      Objective: Put every SEC request from every pipeline behind one storage-backed renewable lease and rate budget.
      Outcomes: O8
      Consumes: Stage 2 fetcher; Stage 3 and Stage 5 workflows
      Produces: a collector lease with daily-first turn order and lease-loss stop
      Exit: O8 — concurrent backfill, daily and reconciliation collectors never exceed the configured rate together, and a takeover after lease loss creates no overlapping request issuer
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: Azure deployment and configuration
      Objective: Deploy the shared image to an isolated Azure environment with ADF orchestration and typed, validated configuration, triggers disabled.
      Outcomes: O4, O11
      Consumes: Stages 2–6
      Produces: scheduling and deployment (infrastructure as code, managed identities, ADF pipelines, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS and Table Storage backends); `conf/sec-edgar-ingest.yaml`
      Exit: O4 — ADF starts and polls a job to a terminal outcome, an ambiguous start halts without relaunch, and the bounded live smoke test of §7 step 4 records its measurements; O11 — invalid configuration is refused before any network request, with §4.8 starting values in place
      Leaves out: trigger enablement (Stage 9)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Validation suite, traceability and runbooks
      Objective: Bring every outcome to the §6 test standard and the §4.7 and §8 operational standard.
      Outcomes: O1–O11 (full standard)
      Consumes: Stage 7 isolated environment
      Produces: full validation suites (§6 CI and integration tests); traceability (structured logs, run reports, alerts); runbooks
      Exit: every §6 CI exit-criteria group passes on fixtures and mocks; integration tests pass on isolated Azure resources; each §4.7 alert fires on its injected fault; §7 step 5 replay and rollback rehearsal recorded
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 9: Baseline campaign and scheduled operation
      Objective: Run the production backfill, daily catch-up and first reconciliation, then enable triggers.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O7 (production)
      Consumes: Stage 8 passing suite and runbooks; range, handoff date and SEC identity recorded per §7 step 1
      Produces: an active production catalog; a release record
      Exit: §7 Exit — every requested baseline unit published or the incomplete range recorded; daily trigger enabled after accepted catch-up; reconciliation run once manually then on schedule; observed scheduled runs recorded with image and configuration versions
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the
> stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, run derive-roadmap §6 over O1–O11, with evidence per verdict (implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, deferred items). Every numbered spec requirement, R1–R11, is cited by an outcome's Spec cell; any found uncited at completion is listed as unmet. Unmet outcomes exit as a new stage or a written deferral.
